submissions.title: NVIDIA Guarantees SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio to Exclusively Host NVIDIA AI Compute
submissions.excerpt: NVIDIA entered into guarantees to secure approximately 4.25 gigawatts (GW) at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT — not currently tracked. Distinct from the already-tracked 'Stargate Lordstown' (slug stargate-lordstown-ohio), which is a separate Oracle-owned site in Trumbull County, NE Ohio. This is SB Energy's (SoftBank subsidiary) PORTS-Pike Technology Campus near Piketon, Pike County — a former uranium-enrichment site. OpenAI is the 20-year tenant for up to ~8GW of an eventual ~10GW campus; NVIDIA will exclusively supply AI compute. Phase 1 is ~4.25GW, first power targeted FY2029, full buildout ~2032. IMPORTANT: the widely-reported '$105 billion' figure is a CONTINGENT RESIDUAL-VALUE GUARANTEE cap (NVIDIA credit support if OpenAI defaults/insolvency events occur) — it is NOT capex and should not be entered as capexUsd. No confirmed capex figure found. submissions.title: New Texas data center projects frozen until state audits them
submissions.excerpt: directing the PUCT and ERCOT to conduct a 'comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT's interconnection process'
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: statewide, not tied to a single project. Gov. Abbott (Aug 3, 2026 letter to PUCT/ERCOT) ordered a freeze: no new data center may advance in ERCOT's interconnection queue until PUCT/ERCOT complete an audit of ~250-300 queued projects (energy, water use, tax breaks, ownership, community-impact disclosures). ERCOT says the audit will take 'several months' (reporting points to ~Dec 2026). Any project failing to comply is denied grid connection. This plausibly touches many tracked Texas projects still awaiting interconnection: IREN Childress/Sweetwater, Fluidstack Abernathy, Cipher Black Pearl, Crusoe Goodnight/Abilene Clean Campus, Aligned Caprock, Stargate Milam County/Shackelford County, Microsoft Pecos, QTS-Lancium Hall County, CyrusOne Freestone. Per Texas Tribune follow-up (Aug 14), the audit's practical scope/enforcement mechanism remained vague even as officials touted it — flagging for reviewer judgment on whether/how to reflect per-project status; this does not appear to halt construction already underway with an existing interconnection agreement, but that distinction needs per-project confirmation. submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Fort Worth, TX. submissions.title: Durham County adopts 9-month pause on data centers
submissions.excerpt: Durham County commissioners voted 4-1 to adopt a nine-month moratorium on new large-scale data centers
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Durham County, NC. Exempts facilities under 100,000 sq ft that use closed-loop cooling and no diesel backup generators. No tracked project appears to be sited in Durham County currently; logging as a new regional restriction data point for the siting-restrictions dataset. submissions.title: Meta can keep its data center details private, PSC decides
submissions.excerpt: The Louisiana Public Service Commission voted 3-1 to overrule its administrative judge's order requiring Meta to disclose
submissions.note: Regulatory update on tracked Meta Hyperion project — not a new construction/siting restriction, the reverse: the PSC BLOCKED disclosure. Commission voted 3-1 along party lines (Aug 12) to overturn its administrative law judge's July 10 subpoena order, letting Meta keep confidential the methodology behind the power-need and job-creation figures Entergy cited in its applications to build new gas turbines for Hyperion. Practical effect: none of the publicly cited MW/jobs figures for Hyperion have been independently verified through discovery, and now likely won't be. Tracker should continue treating Hyperion's power figures as company-stated estimates (as the existing analyst notes already do), not confirmed.
